source.section: Instructions PDF pp.9-10, Schedule M line 1t, questions 1 and 2 and table lines 1-4; Worksheet Step 1 lines 1-7, Step 2 lines 8-13 and instructions PDF p.9, Schedule M line 1s; Instructions PDF p.4, RI-1040 lines 1-5; PDF p.5, lines 6-8; PDF p.13, Tax Computation Worksheet ('Use for all filing status types')

worked: Federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 49,950.00 + taxable Social Security 34,000.00 + interest 49,800.00 = 133,750.00. Federal taxable income = 133,750.00 - 31,500.00 standard deduction - 1 x 1,600.00 age 65+ = 100,650.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). RI-1040 line 1 federal AGI 133,750.00. Line 1s, Social Security worksheet: person 0 born 1955-06-15 (age 70). Line 3 federal AGI 133,750.00; line 4 Qualifying widow(er); line 5 born on or before 03/01/1959: yes; line 6 133,750.00; line 7 133,750.00 less than 133,750.00: no. STOP: not eligible; modification 0.00. Line 1t: question 1 born on or before March 1, 1959: person 0 born 1955-06-15 (age 70): yes; question 2 federal AGI 133,750.00 less than or equal to 133,750.00: yes. Table: person 0 line 2 49,950.00, line 3 lesser of that and 50,000.00 = 49,950.00; line 4 = 49,950.00. Line 1y total decreasing modifications = 49,950.00. Line 2a other-state obligations 0.00; line 2m total increasing modifications = 0.00. Schedule M page 2 line 3 net = 0.00 - 49,950.00 = -49,950.00; RI-1040 line 2 = -49,950.00. Line 3 modified federal AGI = 133,750.00 + (-49,950.00) = 83,800.00. Standard Deduction and Exemption Worksheets: line 3 83,800.00 is not more than 254,250.00: the worksheets stop at line 3, full amounts. Line 4 standard deduction: 21,800.00 (Qualifying widow(er)). Line 5 = 83,800.00 - 21,800.00 = 62,000.00. Line 6 exemptions: 1 x 5,100.00 = 5,100.00. Line 7 taxable income = 62,000.00 - 5,100.00 = 56,900.00. Line 8 tax on 56,900.00 by the schedule as numbers: 56,900.00 x 0.0375 = 2133.750000 = 2,133.75. Credits 0.00 (Schedule I, Schedule II, RI earned income credit and RI-1040H are not modelled and not claimed here). Rhode Island income tax = 2,133.75. Note: Qualifying widow(er) at exactly 133,750.
accepted_approximations: The pension test keeps the relief at exactly the limit, as instructions line 1t asks ('less than or equal to'); the statute printed in the Guide says 'less than'.
